strengths: Diversified generation mix across thermal, hydro and renewables plus an early, growing push into battery storage positions it across multiple parts of this sector at once
risks: Aggressive capacity expansion across generation types and storage is funded substantially by debt

waareeEnergy.name: Waaree Energies
strengths: India's largest solar module manufacturer by capacity, with a growing order book and an expanding export business to the US
risks: Recently listed (Oct 2024) with limited multi-year financial track record

f.note: Listed Oct 2024

sterlingWilsonEnergy.name: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy
strengths: India's largest pure-play solar EPC contractor by track record, now past its earlier financial-stress period with a recovering order book
risks: History of financial stress and governance concerns a few years ago - balance sheet recovery is still relatively recent

f.note: Recovering from a prior period of financial stress; FY26 slipped back to a net loss

adaniGreenEnergy.name: Adani Green Energy
adaniGreenEnergy.role: One of India's largest renewable (solar + wind) IPPs
strengths: One of India's largest contracted renewable generation portfolios by operating capacity, spanning both solar and wind with long-dated PPAs underpinning revenue visibility
risks: High leverage funding its aggressive capacity build-out
Group-level financing/governance scrutiny has periodically pressured Adani group stock sentiment

suzlon.name: Suzlon Energy
strengths: India's largest domestic wind turbine OEM, now past its earlier debt-driven financial stress with a deleveraged balance sheet and recovering order book
risks: History of severe financial stress and balance-sheet restructuring - the turnaround, while real, is still relatively recent

f.note: FY23 profit includes a one-off gain on debt restructuring and FY25 a deferred-tax credit, not run-rate

inoxWind.name: Inox Wind
strengths: Established domestic wind turbine manufacturing base with an improving balance sheet and growing order book as the wind sector recovers
risks: Smaller scale and thinner balance sheet than the market-leading domestic OEM
History of financial stress in the broader Inox Wind group

orientGreen.name: Orient Green Power
strengths: Established, long-operating wind generation asset base gives steady, if modest, recurring PPA revenue
risks: Small-cap with thin trading liquidity and a much smaller, less diversified asset base than large conglomerate-backed peers

f.note: Small-cap

bhelHydro.name: Bharat Heavy Electricals
bhelHydro.role: Hydro turbines, generators and EPC for conventional and pumped-storage hydro plants
strengths: Decades of installed hydro turbine base across India's PSU hydro fleet position it for both renovation orders and new pumped-storage project awards
risks: Hydro/PSP equipment is one of several business lines within a broader, historically thin-margin PSU equipment manufacturer

nhpc.name: NHPC
strengths: India's largest dedicated hydropower generator with regulated, cost-plus-return tariffs and a growing pumped-storage project pipeline
risks: Monsoon-dependent generation variability year to year
New large hydro sites are increasingly scarce and face longer environmental/land-acquisition timelines

sjvn.name: SJVN
sjvn.role: PSU hydropower generator, expanding into solar, wind and pumped storage
strengths: Established PSU hydro generator diversifying into solar, wind and pumped storage, giving exposure across multiple generation types under one regulated balance sheet
risks: Smaller scale than NHPC with a similarly monsoon-dependent core hydro business
Diversification into renewables/storage is still early-stage relative to its legacy hydro base

exideEnergy.name: Exide Industries
exideEnergy.role: Li-ion cells and grid-scale battery energy storage systems via Exide Energy Solutions
strengths: Long-established battery brand and distribution network to lean on while scaling the Exide Energy Solutions Li-ion gigafactory into grid-scale BESS
risks: Li-ion and grid-scale BESS business sits in a separate subsidiary, still small relative to the core lead-acid battery business

f.note: FY22 profit includes a one-time gain

amararajaEnergy.name: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility
amararajaEnergy.role: Li-ion cells and energy-storage systems via Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies
strengths: Established lead-acid battery manufacturing and distribution base to lean on while scaling the Advanced Cell Technologies Li-ion business into grid-scale storage
risks: Li-ion and grid-scale storage business runs through a separate subsidiary, still small relative to the core lead-acid business

greenko.name: Greenko Group
greenko.role: Large pumped-storage and renewable-plus-storage project developer
strengths: One of India's largest dedicated pumped-storage and renewable-plus-storage developers, with a project pipeline few domestic peers can match
risks: Privately held (Singapore-domiciled holding structure) - no India-listed public financials; figures here are not available
notes: Privately held; Hyderabad-founded, backed by GIC and ADIA among other investors
One of India's largest pumped-storage and round-the-clock renewable project developers
No India-listed public market data - not listed

tataPowerEnergy.name: Tata Power
tataPowerEnergy.role: Diversified generation across thermal, hydro (incl. pumped storage), solar and wind, plus transmission & distribution
strengths: Rare fully diversified listed generation portfolio spanning thermal, hydro/pumped-storage, solar and wind, backed by a large integrated T&D business
risks: Generation is spread thin across many technologies within a much larger diversified T&D and power-generation business - no single segment dominates

godrejProp.name: Godrej Properties
godrejProp.role: Pan-India residential developer, largely through joint-development and outright land deals in MMR, NCR, Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad
strengths: Largest Indian developer by booking value for three years running: record FY26 bookings of Rs 34,171 Cr (+16%), beating guidance by 5%
Record FY26 operating cash flow (~Rs 7,830 Cr) and FY27 bookings guidance of Rs 39,000 Cr
Godrej brand and a multi-city land pipeline added through JDAs and outright buys
risks: Reported profit lags bookings because revenue is recognised on completion; reported ROE is still single-digit
Aggressive land buying lifts net debt if sales slow
Stock down ~27% over the past year as the housing cycle cooled

dlf.name: DLF
dlf.role: Largest listed developer by market value: luxury housing in Gurugram plus a large office and mall rental business through DCCDL (a JV with GIC)
strengths: Net cash of Rs 14,155 Cr at Mar 2026 with zero gross debt in the development business
FY26 bookings of Rs 20,143 Cr; large low-cost Gurugram land bank supports high-margin luxury launches
Rental arm (DCCDL) adds steady office and mall income
risks: Bookings are lumpy: Q1 FY27 pre-sales were only ~Rs 657 Cr as launches were deferred
Heavy concentration in Gurugram luxury housing
FY27 guidance (Rs 20,000 Cr) depends on launches still pending

prestige.name: Prestige Estates Projects
prestige.role: Bengaluru-based developer of homes, offices, malls (Forum) and hotels, now expanding in MMR, NCR and Hyderabad
strengths: Record FY26 sales of Rs 30,024 Cr, up 76% - the second-largest listed seller
Diversified rental base across office, retail and hospitality grows annuity income
Large launch pipeline across multiple cities
risks: Capital-heavy office, mall and hotel build-out raises debt
Execution risk as it scales in new cities outside Bengaluru
Profit has been volatile (FY25 net profit fell to Rs 617 Cr)

lodha.name: Lodha Developers (Macrotech)
lodha.role: Largest MMR residential developer, also in Pune and Bengaluru, with a large land bank and industrial/data-centre park at Palava
strengths: FY26 pre-sales of Rs 20,530 Cr (+16%) with record Q4 of Rs 5,890 Cr
Added 12 projects worth ~Rs 60,000 Cr GDV in FY26 - 2.4x its original plan
Land bank at Palava supports housing, industrial parks and data centres for years
risks: Missed FY26 guidance of Rs 21,000 Cr as March sales were deferred
Heavy MMR concentration
History of high leverage, now reduced; the new focus is free cash flow

oberoi.name: Oberoi Realty
oberoi.role: Mumbai developer of luxury homes, offices (Commerz), malls and hotels
strengths: Among the highest margins and ROCE (~17%) in the listed sector
Growing rental income from Mumbai offices and malls (Oberoi Mall, Sky City)
Low debt and long-held, low-cost Mumbai land
risks: FY26 bookings rose only 4% to Rs 5,447 Cr - growth depends on a few large launches
Entirely Mumbai-focused
Board approved raising up to Rs 6,000 Cr, which could dilute shareholders

signature.name: Signatureglobal (India)
signature.role: Gurugram developer focused on mid-income and affordable group housing
strengths: Scaled fast in Gurugram's southern corridors (Sohna, Dwarka Expressway)
Collections of about Rs 4,000 Cr in FY26
risks: FY26 pre-sales of Rs 8,220 Cr fell well short of its Rs 12,500 Cr guidance
Thin operating margins; FY26 profit was driven by one-off other income
Single-city exposure and higher sensitivity to home-loan rates

sobha.name: Sobha

Backward integration gives quality control and a strong delivery reputation
Entered Mumbai luxury housing in FY26

Bengaluru concentration
Integrated model ties up capital in manufacturing units

brigade.name: Brigade Enterprises
brigade.role: South India developer of homes, office parks (WTC), malls (Orion) and hotels

Strong brand in Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad
Hotel arm listed separately (Brigade Hotel Ventures, 2025)

Rental assets add debt during build-out
Stock down ~20% in a year as housing sentiment weakened

mahindraLifespace.name: Mahindra Lifespace Developers
mahindraLifespace.role: Mahindra group developer of homes and integrated industrial cities and clusters (Mahindra World City, Origins)

Mahindra brand and parent support

risks: Still small; revenue and profit swing with project completions
Housing pre-sales scale is far below the leaders
Industrial land sales are lumpy

anantRaj.name: Anant Raj
anantRaj.role: Delhi-NCR land owner and developer of housing, and a builder of data-centre and IT-park capacity on its own land

Data-centre business on existing campuses adds a rental-style income stream
risks: Data-centre plans need heavy capex and anchor tenants
Concentrated in Delhi-NCR
Stock has been volatile after a large multi-year rally

Hotels add more volatile income

Large Hyderabad and Bengaluru exposure to GCC demand

Units trade in a Rs 108-129 range, not far above the Rs 100 issue price
